nampt.label: NAMPT
nampt.function: Nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase; rate-limiting enzyme of the NAD+ salvage pathway, converts NAM to NMN.
nampt.aging_relevance: NAMPT/NAD+ decline with age in multiple tissues; AMPK- and CR-inducible node controlling SIRT1 activity.
nampt.human_evidence: NAMPT and NAD+ decrease in aged human tissues (reviewed); mechanistic data mostly rodent/cell.

nmnat1.label: NMNAT1
nmnat1.function: Nicotinamide/nicotinic acid mononucleotide adenylyltransferase; converts NMN to NAD+ (family NMNAT1/2/3).
nmnat1.aging_relevance: Obligatory final step of NAD+ synthesis; not rate-limiting but essential.

nmrk1.label: NMRK1
nmrk1.function: Nicotinamide riboside kinase 1 (NRK1); phosphorylates NR to NMN, enabling the Preiss-Handler-independent route to NAD+.
nmrk1.aging_relevance: Required for NR-based NAD+ repletion strategies.
nmrk1.human_evidence: Human NRK1 identified and shown essential for NR utilisation.

nam.label: NAM
nam.function: Nicotinamide; NAD+ salvage precursor and substrate of NAMPT; also a product/feedback inhibitor of sirtuins.
nam.aging_relevance: Central salvage metabolite; its methylation by NNMT diverts it from NAD+ synthesis.

nmn.label: NMN
nmn.function: Nicotinamide mononucleotide; key NAD+ intermediate, product of NAMPT and NMRK1, substrate of NMNAT; used as a supplement.
nmn.aging_relevance: Supplementation restores NAD+ and improves age-related physiology in mice and insulin sensitivity in humans.
nmn.human_evidence: RCT: NMN improves muscle insulin sensitivity in prediabetic women (Yoshino 2021).

nr.label: NR
nr.function: Nicotinamide riboside; NAD+ precursor vitamin, phosphorylated by NMRK1 to NMN; orally bioavailable.
nr.aging_relevance: Raises blood NAD+ in middle-aged/older humans; well tolerated.
nr.human_evidence: Human trials (Trammell 2016, Martens 2018) show dose-dependent NAD+ elevation.

nad+.label: NAD+
nad+.function: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide; redox cofactor and obligate co-substrate for sirtuins, PARPs, CD38 and SARM1.
nad+.aging_relevance: Declines with age in rodents (human evidence more limited); its restoration improves healthspan in mice.
nad+.human_evidence: Age-related decline inconsistently observed in humans; precursor supplementation raises NAD+ (reviewed Vinten 2025).

parp1.label: PARP1
parp1.function: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase 1; major NAD+-consuming enzyme activated by DNA damage.
parp1.aging_relevance: PARP1 activation lowers NAD+ and SIRT1 activity; PARP1 deletion raises NAD+ and mitochondrial function.

cd38.label: CD38
cd38.function: NAD+ glycohydrolase/ADP-ribosyl cyclase; main NADase driving age-related NAD+ decline and degrading NMN.
cd38.aging_relevance: CD38 expression/activity rises with age on M1-like macrophages; CD38 KO or inhibition preserves NAD+.
cd38.human_evidence: Human ecto-enzyme; aging data from mice and human senescent-cell/SASP models.

sarm1.label: SARM1
sarm1.function: Sterile alpha and TIR motif protein 1; intrinsic NAD+ hydrolase (TIR domain) executing axon degeneration.
sarm1.aging_relevance: Context-specific NAD+ consumer relevant to neurodegeneration rather than blood prevention.
sarm1.human_evidence: Human enzyme; activity shown with purified protein.

nnmt.label: NNMT
nnmt.function: Nicotinamide N-methyltransferase; methylates NAM to 1-methylnicotinamide using SAM, diverting NAM from NAD+ salvage.
nnmt.aging_relevance: Elevated in obesity/metabolic disease; knockdown raises NAD+ and energy expenditure.

inflammaging.label: Inflammaging
inflammaging.function: Chronic low-grade sterile inflammation of ageing (SASP, inflammatory cytokines) feeding into the NAD+ axis.
inflammaging.aging_relevance: Senescent-cell SASP induces CD38+ macrophages that degrade NAD+.
inflammaging.human_evidence: Human senescent cells/SASP characterised; causal NAD+ link from mouse models.

sirt1.label: SIRT1
sirt1.function: NAD+-dependent class III deacetylase; hub integrating nutrient/NAD+ status to PGC-1a, FOXO, p53, NF-kB, LKB1. | NAD+-dependent deacetylase; induced by caloric restriction serum; promotes cell survival (deacetylates Ku70). | NAD+-dependent deacetylase; downstream of AMPK-driven NAD+ increase; deacetylates PGC-1alpha.
sirt1.aging_relevance: Central longevity deacetylase; activity tracks NAD+ availability. | Proposed mediator of CR lifespan benefits; induced by CR in rats and human cells (Cohen 2004). | Core longevity-associated sirtuin; activated by FGF21 via raised NAD+.
sirt1.human_evidence: Human enzyme; downstream effects mostly cellular/rodent. | Human cells exposed to CR serum show SIRT1 induction. | Human metabolic/longevity signalling.

sirt3.label: SIRT3
sirt3.function: Mitochondrial NAD+-dependent deacetylase; deacetylates and activates SOD2 and other metabolic enzymes.
sirt3.aging_relevance: Mediates CR-induced reduction of oxidative stress; tumour suppressor.
sirt3.human_evidence: Human enzyme; reduced SIRT3 in human cancers.

sirt6.label: SIRT6
sirt6.function: NAD+-dependent H3K9/H3K56 deacetylase and mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase; genome stability and NF-kB attenuation.
sirt6.aging_relevance: Overexpression extends mouse lifespan/healthspan; deficiency causes premature ageing.
sirt6.human_evidence: Human enzyme; lifespan data from transgenic mice.

ppargc1a.label: PPARGC1A
ppargc1a.function: PGC-1alpha; transcriptional coactivator of mitochondrial biogenesis and oxidative metabolism; deacetylated/activated by SIRT1. | PGC-1alpha; master coactivator of mitochondrial biogenesis; directly phosphorylated/activated by AMPK (T177/S538). | PGC-1alpha, master transcriptional coactivator of mitochondrial biogenesis and oxidative metabolism; activated by AMPK-SIRT1.
ppargc1a.aging_relevance: Links NAD+/SIRT1 to mitochondrial function and gluconeogenesis. | Mitochondrial biogenesis declines with age; PGC-1alpha mediates exercise/CR/AMPK benefits. | Drives mitochondrial oxidative capacity; downstream effector of FGF21/AMPK/SIRT1.
ppargc1a.human_evidence: Human coactivator; mechanism shown in rodent tissue/cells. | Primary muscle cells and KO mice (Jager 2007). | Human mitochondrial biogenesis regulator.

foxo3.label: FOXO3
foxo3.function: Forkhead transcription factor; deacetylated by SIRT1, promoting stress resistance over apoptosis. | Forkhead transcription factor; phosphorylated by Akt (T32/S253) causing 14-3-3 binding and nuclear exclusion; drives autophagy, stress-resistance and antioxidant genes.
foxo3.aging_relevance: Human longevity-associated locus; downstream of insulin/NAD+ signalling. | FOXO3 genotype robustly associated with human longevity (Willcox 2008; Flachsbart 2009); orthologue of C. elegans DAF-16.
foxo3.human_evidence: FOXO3 variants associated with human longevity; mechanism cellular. | FOXO3A SNPs associated with longevity in Japanese, German and French cohorts.

p53.label: p53
p53.function: Tumour suppressor transcription factor; acetylation at K382 activates it, SIRT1 deacetylates and dampens it.
p53.aging_relevance: Node linking NAD+/sirtuins to apoptosis/senescence balance.
p53.human_evidence: Human protein; deacetylation shown in human cells.

nf-kb.label: NF-kB
nf-kb.function: Pro-inflammatory transcription factor (RelA/p65); inhibited by SIRT1 (K310 deacetylation) and SIRT6 (H3K9 deacetylation at target promoters).

lkb1.label: LKB1
lkb1.function: Master upstream kinase of AMPK; deacetylated by SIRT1 (K48), increasing its activity and cytoplasmic localisation.
lkb1.aging_relevance: Couples SIRT1/NAD+ to AMPK energy sensing.
lkb1.human_evidence: Human kinase; SIRT1 regulation shown in cells and rodent liver.

ampk.label: AMPK
ampk.function: AMP-activated protein kinase; energy sensor that induces NAMPT/NAD+ and thereby SIRT1. | Energy-sensing kinase; activated by low energy/CR/metformin; phosphorylates TSC2, RAPTOR, ULK1, PGC-1alpha. | Cellular energy sensor; activated by raised AMP/ADP and by LKB1; central hub of the nutrient-sensing network.
ampk.aging_relevance: Feedback loop partner of SIRT1 in the nutrient-sensing network. | Conserved mediator of CR longevity (AMPK-FOXO in C. elegans; CR-mimetic transcriptome). | Activation mimics caloric restriction and extends lifespan in model organisms; target of FGF21 and canagliflozin.
ampk.human_evidence: Human kinase; NAD+/SIRT1 coupling shown in mouse muscle. | Human/animal mechanistic and intervention data. | Human drug target (metformin, canagliflozin pathway).

sod2.label: SOD2
sod2.function: Manganese superoxide dismutase (MnSOD); scavenges mitochondrial superoxide; activated by SIRT3 deacetylation (K68/K122).
sod2.aging_relevance: Effector of CR/SIRT3-mediated oxidative stress reduction.
sod2.human_evidence: Human enzyme; deacetylation sites conserved, shown in mouse.

ros.label: ROS
ros.function: Reactive oxygen species (mitochondrial superoxide); reduced by SOD2 activity.

lifespan_extension.label: Lifespan_extension
lifespan_extension.function: Phenotypic output: extension of mammalian lifespan/healthspan. | Phenotype node: extension of median/maximal lifespan (strong mouse/genetic data).
lifespan_extension.aging_relevance: Primary longevity readout; used only for strong genetic/mouse data. | Primary longevity outcome.
lifespan_extension.human_evidence: Mouse transgenic data (SIRT6). | Inferred from mammalian models.

insulin_sensitivity.label: Insulin_sensitivity
insulin_sensitivity.function: Phenotypic output: tissue insulin sensitivity / glucose disposal. | Whole-body/tissue responsiveness to insulin; enhanced by DR and S6K1 loss, impaired by chronic rapamycin (mTORC2 loss). | Phenotype node: whole-body/tissue insulin sensitivity.
insulin_sensitivity.aging_relevance: Blood-readable age-related phenotype improved by NAD+ precursors. | Improved insulin sensitivity is a core blood-readable healthspan outcome of CR and S6K1/mTOR manipulation. | Improved insulin sensitivity is a healthspan-associated readout.
insulin_sensitivity.human_evidence: Human RCT: NMN improves muscle insulin sensitivity. | CALERIE improved insulin sensitivity index (Kraus 2019). | Human metabolic outcome.

78c.label: 78c
78c.function: Thiazoloquin(az)olin(on)e CD38 inhibitor; reverses tissue NAD+ decline.
78c.aging_relevance: Improves glucose tolerance, muscle and cardiac function in aged mice.

resveratrol.label: Resveratrol
resveratrol.function: Polyphenol; reported SIRT1 activator (substrate/fluorophore-dependent) and AMPK activator via PDE inhibition.
resveratrol.human_evidence: Human supplement; direct SIRT1 activation disputed.

insulin.label: Insulin
insulin.function: Anabolic hormone; ligand of INSR, activates PI3K-Akt and mTORC1; lower fasting insulin is a hallmark of dietary restriction and improved insulin sensitivity.
insulin.aging_relevance: Lower circulating insulin associates with longevity; reduced insulin/IGF signalling extends lifespan across taxa.
insulin.human_evidence: Fasting insulin lowered by long-term CR in humans (Fontana 2004).

insr.label: INSR
insr.function: Insulin receptor tyrosine kinase; autophosphorylates on insulin binding and phosphorylates IRS1.
insr.aging_relevance: Core node of insulin/IGF signalling axis implicated in ageing.
insr.human_evidence: Insulin-stimulated receptor autophosphorylation shown in human lymphocytes (Kasuga 1982).

irs1.label: IRS1
irs1.function: Docking adaptor downstream of INSR/IGF1R; tyrosine-phosphorylated IRS1 binds and activates PI3K; node of S6K1 negative feedback (Ser1101).
irs1.aging_relevance: Hub of insulin/IGF signalling and of the mTOR-S6K1 feedback loop central to nutrient sensing and ageing.
irs1.human_evidence: S6K1-mediated IRS1 Ser1101 phosphorylation and insulin resistance demonstrated in humans (Tremblay 2007).

pi3k.label: PI3K
pi3k.function: Phosphoinositide 3-kinase; activated by tyrosine-phosphorylated IRS1 via p85 SH2 domains; generates PIP3 to activate Akt.

igf1.label: IGF1
igf1.function: Insulin-like growth factor 1; ligand of IGF1R activating IRS1-PI3K-Akt; reduced by protein restriction in humans. | Insulin-like growth factor 1; principal somatic growth mediator of GH, downstream STAT5 target in liver.
igf1.aging_relevance: Reduced IGF-1 signalling extends lifespan in model organisms; blood-readable biomarker of nutrient/protein status. | Reduced GH/IGF-1 signalling is strongly associated with longevity; FGF21 induces GH resistance and lowers IGF-1.
igf1.human_evidence: Serum IGF-1 lowered by protein restriction but not CR-alone in humans (Fontana 2008). | Human blood biomarker; low IGF-1 signalling linked to human longevity.

igf1r.label: IGF1R
igf1r.function: IGF-1 receptor tyrosine kinase; phosphorylates IRS1 on ligand binding.
igf1r.aging_relevance: Igf1r+/- mice live ~26% longer with greater oxidative-stress resistance (Holzenberger 2003); central regulator of mammalian lifespan.
igf1r.human_evidence: IGF1R mutations enriched in human centenarians (literature); mouse lifespan data.

akt.label: Akt
akt.function: Serine/threonine kinase; activated by PI3K (T308) and mTORC2 (S473); phosphorylates FOXO3, TSC2, MDM2.
akt.aging_relevance: Central effector of insulin/IGF signalling; suppresses FOXO and activates mTORC1.
akt.human_evidence: Human cell mechanistic data; Akt2 essential for glucose homeostasis (mouse).

tsc2.label: TSC2
tsc2.function: Tuberin; GAP for RHEB; inhibited by Akt phosphorylation (T1462), activated by AMPK; gatekeeper of mTORC1.
tsc2.aging_relevance: Integrator of growth-factor and energy signals onto mTORC1.

rheb.label: RHEB
rheb.function: Ras-family GTPase; GTP-RHEB directly binds and activates mTORC1; inhibited by TSC2 GAP activity.
rheb.aging_relevance: Obligatory activator of mTORC1, the central nutrient-sensing kinase in ageing.

mtor.label: mTOR
mtor.function: mTORC1 catalytic kinase (with RAPTOR); activated by RHEB; phosphorylates S6K1 (T389), 4E-BP1 (T37/46), TFEB (S211) and ULK1; inhibited by rapamycin-FKBP12.
mtor.aging_relevance: Rapamycin inhibition of mTORC1 extends lifespan in genetically heterogeneous mice even when started late (Harrison 2009).
mtor.human_evidence: Human cell mechanism; drug target in trials.

rps6kb1.label: RPS6KB1
rps6kb1.function: p70 S6 kinase 1 (S6K1); mTORC1 substrate (T389); promotes protein synthesis; phosphorylates IRS1 (S1101) in negative feedback.
rps6kb1.aging_relevance: S6K1-deficient mice are long-lived, insulin-sensitive and CR-mimetic (Selman 2009; Um 2004).
rps6kb1.human_evidence: S6K1-IRS1 Ser1101 feedback shown in humans (Tremblay 2007).

eif4ebp1.label: EIF4EBP1
eif4ebp1.function: 4E-BP1; translational repressor that binds eIF4E; phosphorylation by mTORC1 (T37/46 priming) releases eIF4E to permit cap-dependent translation.
eif4ebp1.aging_relevance: 4E-BP mediates lifespan effects of reduced TOR in flies; translational output node.

tfeb.label: TFEB
tfeb.function: Master transcription factor of lysosomal/autophagy genes; phosphorylated by mTORC1 (S211) causing 14-3-3 binding and cytoplasmic retention; mTORC1 inhibition drives its nuclear translocation.
tfeb.aging_relevance: Links mTORC1 inhibition to transcriptional autophagy induction, a conserved pro-longevity program.

mtorc2.label: mTORC2
mtorc2.function: Rapamycin-insensitive mTOR complex 2 (RICTOR-defined); phosphorylates Akt on S473; required for insulin suppression of hepatic gluconeogenesis.
mtorc2.aging_relevance: Chronic rapamycin disrupts mTORC2, causing insulin resistance uncoupled from longevity (Lamming 2012).
mtorc2.human_evidence: Human cell mechanism; mouse in vivo.

rapamycin.label: Rapamycin
rapamycin.function: mTORC1 inhibitor (FKBP12-dependent); chronic dosing also disrupts mTORC2. | Macrolide mTORC1 inhibitor (via FKBP12); rapalogs include everolimus. Inhibits mTOR-driven growth, protein synthesis and immunosenescence.
rapamycin.aging_relevance: Extends median/maximal lifespan in genetically heterogeneous mice even started at 600 days (Harrison 2009). | Canonical mTOR-inhibiting geroprotector (extends lifespan in ITP mice); mTOR inhibition improves immune/vaccine response in the elderly but impairs wound healing in some clinical settings.
rapamycin.human_evidence: Mouse lifespan; human immunosuppressant/geroprotector trials. | Everolimus RCT improved influenza vaccine response in elderly; sirolimus RCT/clinical data on wound-healing complications.

metformin.label: Metformin
metformin.function: Biguanide; inhibits mitochondrial complex I, activates AMPK, raises GDF15; anti-hyperglycaemic.
metformin.aging_relevance: Improves healthspan/lifespan in male mice (Martin-Montalvo 2013); but alone did not extend lifespan in NIA ITP (Strong 2016) - conflicting.
metformin.human_evidence: Widely used anti-diabetic; GDF15 induction shown in human RCTs (Coll 2020); TAME trial ongoing.

complex_i.label: Complex_I
complex_i.function: Mitochondrial respiratory chain NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase (complex I); primary molecular target of metformin.
complex_i.aging_relevance: Partial complex I inhibition lowers cellular energy charge, activating AMPK; mitohormetic.

gdf15.label: GDF15
gdf15.function: Growth/differentiation factor 15; stress cytokine secreted in response to metformin; acts on brainstem GFRAL to reduce food intake.
gdf15.aging_relevance: Blood-readable biomarker rising with metformin and age; mediates metformin's weight/energy-balance effects.
gdf15.human_evidence: Elevated by metformin in two human RCTs (Coll 2020).

dietary_restriction.label: Dietary_restriction
dietary_restriction.function: Reduced calorie (and/or protein) intake without malnutrition; upstream input activating AMPK/FOXO, inhibiting mTOR/insulin/IGF, inducing SIRT1 and autophagy. | Input node for caloric/protein restriction and fasting; canonical pro-longevity dietary intervention that reprograms nutrient-sensing pathways.
dietary_restriction.aging_relevance: Most robust environmental lifespan/healthspan intervention across taxa; CALERIE human trial slowed DunedinPACE of aging (Waziry 2023). | Extends lifespan/healthspan across species and improves metabolic markers in human trials (CALERIE); also carries adverse effects (infection susceptibility, cold sensitivity, impaired wound healing).
dietary_restriction.human_evidence: CALERIE 2-year RCT improved cardiometabolic risk and insulin sensitivity (Kraus 2019); slowed pace of aging (Waziry 2023). | CALERIE 2-year RCT (metabolic adaptation, reduced thyroid axis/oxidative stress); 28-day low-protein diet raises FGF21 in humans; CR lowers core body temperature in long-term human practitioners.

autophagy.label: Autophagy
autophagy.function: Lysosomal bulk degradation/recycling pathway; output of FOXO3, TFEB, DR and mTOR inhibition.
autophagy.aging_relevance: Required for lifespan extension by DR and TOR inhibition (Hansen 2008).

protein_synthesis.label: Protein_synthesis
protein_synthesis.function: Cap-dependent mRNA translation output of mTORC1 via S6K1 and 4E-BP1.
protein_synthesis.aging_relevance: Reduced translation extends lifespan in flies/worms; mTORC1 output.

mitochondrial_biogenesis.label: Mitochondrial_biogenesis
mitochondrial_biogenesis.function: Generation of new mitochondria driven by PGC-1alpha downstream of AMPK.
mitochondrial_biogenesis.aging_relevance: Declines with age; AMPK-PGC-1alpha axis is a CR/exercise mimetic target.
mitochondrial_biogenesis.human_evidence: Muscle cell and KO mouse data.

fgf21.label: FGF21
fgf21.function: Liver-derived (also adipose) endocrine FGF; starvation/protein-restriction hormone signalling through the betaKlotho-FGFR1c co-receptor complex to coordinate the adaptive fasting response.
fgf21.aging_relevance: Transgenic FGF21 overexpression extends mouse lifespan while blunting GH/IGF-1 signalling; circulating FGF21 is a human blood biomarker.
fgf21.human_evidence: Blood-measurable hormone; induced by protein restriction and fasting/ketogenic diet in humans.

ppara.label: PPARA
ppara.function: Nuclear receptor/transcription factor governing fatty-acid oxidation and ketogenesis during fasting; directly induces hepatic FGF21 transcription.
ppara.aging_relevance: Mediator of the hepatic fasting response upstream of FGF21; mechanistic node.
ppara.human_evidence: Target of fibrate drugs in humans; FGF21 induction pathway conserved.

klb-fgfr1.label: KLB-FGFR1
klb-fgfr1.function: Co-receptor complex of betaKlotho (KLB) with FGF receptor 1c that constitutes the obligate signalling receptor for FGF21; betaKlotho confers tissue-specific FGF21 responsiveness.
klb-fgfr1.aging_relevance: Required transducer of all FGF21 metabolic/longevity actions.
klb-fgfr1.human_evidence: KLB and FGFR1 expressed in human adipose/metabolic tissues.

klb.label: KLB
klb.function: betaKlotho, single-pass transmembrane co-receptor essential for FGF21 (and FGF19) binding/activity.
klb.human_evidence: Human KLB required for FGF21 metabolic activity.

fgfr1.label: FGFR1
fgfr1.function: Fibroblast growth factor receptor 1c; tyrosine-kinase receptor that, bound to betaKlotho, transduces FGF21 signalling (MAPK cascade).
fgfr1.aging_relevance: Signalling receptor for FGF21 metabolic actions.
fgfr1.human_evidence: Expressed in human adipocytes; FGF21 receptor.

semaglutide.label: Semaglutide
semaglutide.function: Long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist; incretin mimetic used for type 2 diabetes and obesity.
semaglutide.aging_relevance: Produces large weight loss and reduces major adverse cardiovascular events in humans without diabetes; emerging geroprotective interest.
semaglutide.human_evidence: STEP 1 (weight loss) and SELECT (cardiovascular outcome) RCTs.

glp1r.label: GLP1R
glp1r.function: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor; Gs-coupled receptor mediating glucose-dependent insulin secretion, appetite/food-intake suppression and cardiovascular effects.
glp1r.aging_relevance: Agonism lowers body weight and cardiovascular event risk in humans.
glp1r.human_evidence: Target of semaglutide in human RCTs.

canagliflozin.label: Canagliflozin
canagliflozin.function: SGLT2 inhibitor (phlorizin-derived) that blocks renal glucose reabsorption; also inhibits mitochondrial complex I to activate AMPK.
canagliflozin.aging_relevance: Extends median lifespan of male genetically heterogeneous mice (ITP); lowers peak glucose.
canagliflozin.human_evidence: Approved human antidiabetic with cardiovascular/renal benefit.

slc5a2.label: SLC5A2
slc5a2.function: Sodium/glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2); mediates renal proximal-tubule glucose reabsorption; molecular target of canagliflozin.
slc5a2.aging_relevance: Pharmacological inhibition lowers glycaemia and extends male mouse lifespan.

glucose.label: Glucose
glucose.function: Blood glucose; nutrient input to insulin/nutrient-sensing pathways.
glucose.aging_relevance: Lowering daily peak glucose is proposed to underlie canagliflozin/acarbose lifespan benefit.

cold_sensitivity.label: Cold_sensitivity
cold_sensitivity.function: Phenotype node: reduced core body temperature / increased cold sensitivity (torpor-like regulated hypothermia).
cold_sensitivity.aging_relevance: Lowered body temperature contributes to CR anti-aging effects but is an adverse/comfort cost.
cold_sensitivity.human_evidence: Lower core body temperature in long-term human CR practitioners.

infection_susceptibility.label: Infection_susceptibility
infection_susceptibility.function: Phenotype node: susceptibility to / impaired survival from primary infection.
infection_susceptibility.aging_relevance: Adverse effect of dietary restriction in aged animals (reduced NK activity, higher viral titers).
infection_susceptibility.human_evidence: Rodent aging data; human relevance inferred.

impaired_wound_healing.label: Impaired_wound_healing
impaired_wound_healing.function: Phenotype node: delayed/complicated cutaneous or surgical wound healing.
impaired_wound_healing.aging_relevance: Adverse effect of mTOR inhibition (sirolimus) and, at review level, of dietary restriction.
impaired_wound_healing.human_evidence: Clinical transplant data for sirolimus; review-level data for CR.

body_weight.label: Body_weight
body_weight.aging_relevance: Weight/adiposity reduction accompanies GLP-1R agonism and FGF21 action and improves cardiometabolic risk.

cardiovascular_events.label: Cardiovascular_events
cardiovascular_events.function: Phenotype node: major adverse cardiovascular events (CV death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke).
cardiovascular_events.aging_relevance: Key age-related clinical outcome reduced by GLP-1R agonism.

vaccine_response.label: Vaccine_response
vaccine_response.function: Phenotype node: adaptive immune / vaccine (influenza) response capacity; inverse of immunosenescence.
vaccine_response.aging_relevance: Improved by mTOR inhibition in the elderly (reduced PD-1+ T cells, enhanced antibody titers).

reactions.mechanism: NAMPT is the rate-limiting enzyme of NAD+ salvage, phosphoribosylating nicotinamide (NAM) to NMN; increased NAMPT dosage raises cellular NAD+ and SIRT1 activity.
reactions.notes: Kinetics (Revollo) establish NAMPT as rate-limiting; Fulco confirms NAMPT induction raises NAD+.

reactions.mechanism: NMNAT (NMNAT1/2/3) adenylyltransferase condenses NMN with ATP to form NAD+; final, obligatory step of NAD+ biosynthesis.
reactions.notes: NMNAT modelled as family label; not rate-limiting but essential.

reactions.mechanism: Nicotinamide riboside kinase 1 (NRK1/NMRK1) phosphorylates NR to NMN, a Preiss-Handler-independent route to NAD+.
reactions.notes: Bieganowski & Brenner identified NRK genes essential for NR->NMN.

reactions.mechanism: NMN is the immediate NAD+ precursor; supplying NMN restores NAD+ pools in metabolic tissues of HFD-fed and aged mice.
reactions.notes: Substrate-availability edge; long-term NMN (Mills) restores tissue NAD+ in normal ageing.

reactions.mechanism: NR is salvaged to NMN via NMRK1 before conversion to NAD+.
reactions.notes: Substrate-flux edge complementing the NMRK1 catalytic edge.

reactions.mechanism: NAM is the NAMPT substrate feeding the salvage pathway toward NMN/NAD+.
reactions.notes: Catalysed by NAMPT (see P1A-001).

reactions.mechanism: PARP1 is a major NAD+-consuming enzyme; its activation/presence lowers the NAD+ pool, and PARP1 deletion or pharmacological inhibition raises NAD+.
reactions.notes: Rajman review corroborates PARP1 as a principal NAD+ consumer in ageing.

reactions.mechanism: By depleting NAD+, PARP1 activity limits SIRT1 deacetylase activity; PARP1 deletion/inhibition increases NAD+ content and SIRT1 activity, phenocopying SIRT1 activation.
reactions.notes: Indirect (NAD+-mediated) inhibition; a key feedback node between NAD+ consumers and sirtuins.

reactions.mechanism: CD38 is an NADase whose expression and activity rise with age and drive the age-related decline in tissue NAD+; CD38 KO preserves NAD+.
reactions.notes: Camacho-Pereira (KO, aged mice) + Rajman review.

reactions.mechanism: CD38 is the main enzyme degrading the NAD+ precursor NMN in vivo, limiting the efficacy of NAD+-replacement therapy.
reactions.notes: Explains CD38 inhibition as a route to boost NMN/NAD+.

reactions.mechanism: The SARM1 TIR domain has intrinsic NAD+ hydrolase activity, cleaving NAD+ into ADPR, cADPR and nicotinamide to execute axonal NAD+ depletion.
reactions.notes: Context-specific (axonal) NAD+ consumer; peripheral to blood-based prevention.

reactions.mechanism: NNMT methylates NAM to 1-methylnicotinamide using SAM, removing NAM from the NAD+ salvage pool; NNMT knockdown raises NAD+ and SAM.
reactions.notes: Reduces substrate (NAM) available to NAMPT; edge sign = depletes NAM.

reactions.mechanism: Senescent-cell SASP cytokines induce proliferation of pro-inflammatory M1-like macrophages that express high CD38 and CD38-dependent NADase activity in metabolic tissues during ageing.
reactions.notes: Links the inflammation module to NAD+ decline via CD38 induction.

reactions.mechanism: SIRT1 is an NAD+-dependent deacetylase; its activity scales with NAD+ availability (raised by NAMPT, lowered by NAD+ consumers).
reactions.notes: Core cofactor dependency and hub of the NAD+-SIRT1 feedback loop.

reactions.mechanism: SIRT3 is the major mitochondrial NAD+-dependent deacetylase; activity depends on mitochondrial NAD+.
reactions.notes: Schwer establishes NAD+ dependence; Qiu links to CR/ageing.

reactions.mechanism: SIRT6 is an NAD+-dependent H3K9 deacetylase; cofactor availability governs its chromatin activity.
reactions.notes: Michishita (enzymology) + Kawahara (NF-kB/ageing).

reactions.mechanism: SIRT1 binds and deacetylates PGC-1alpha at specific lysines in an NAD+-dependent manner, activating gluconeogenic and mitochondrial fatty-acid-oxidation gene programs.
reactions.notes: Two independent groups/tissues.

reactions.mechanism: Under oxidative stress SIRT1 complexes with and deacetylates FOXO3, biasing FOXO3 toward cell-cycle arrest/stress resistance and away from apoptosis.
reactions.notes: Effect sign = activation of stress-resistance arm of FOXO3.

reactions.mechanism: SIRT1/Sir2alpha binds p53 and deacetylates C-terminal K382, reducing p53 transcriptional activity and p53-dependent apoptosis.
reactions.notes: Two independent 2001 Cell papers.

reactions.mechanism: SIRT1 interacts with RelA/p65 and deacetylates K310, inhibiting NF-kB transcriptional activity and sensitising cells to TNF-induced apoptosis.
reactions.notes: Anti-inflammatory arm of SIRT1.

reactions.mechanism: SIRT1 deacetylates LKB1 (K48), increasing its cytoplasmic localisation, STRAD association and kinase activity, thereby activating AMPK.
reactions.notes: Feeds the SIRT1->LKB1->AMPK limb of the loop (AMPK/LKB1 edges exist in map).

reactions.mechanism: AMPK activation induces Nampt transcription/activity, raising the NAD+/NADH ratio; required for glucose-restriction effects on SIRT1.
reactions.notes: Fulco (Sartorelli) + Canto (Auwerx); establishes AMPK->NAD+ arm.

reactions.mechanism: AMPK raises cellular NAD+ levels, enhancing SIRT1 activity and deacetylation of PGC-1alpha/FOXO targets; convergent control of energy metabolism.
reactions.notes: Net (NAD+-mediated) AMPK->SIRT1 edge; closes the AMPK-SIRT1 mutual-activation loop.

reactions.mechanism: SIRT3 deacetylates critical lysines on SOD2/MnSOD, enhancing its antioxidant activity; mediates CR-induced reduction of oxidative stress.
reactions.notes: Two independent groups (Chen; Gius) with site mutants.

reactions.mechanism: Activated SOD2 dismutates mitochondrial superoxide, lowering ROS; SIRT3/SOD2 axis reduces cellular ROS and oxidative damage.
reactions.notes: Connects SIRT3 axis to existing ROS node.

reactions.mechanism: Under oxidative stress SIRT6 associates with PARP1 and mono-ADP-ribosylates it on K521, stimulating PARP1 poly-ADP-ribosylase activity and enhancing double-strand-break repair.
reactions.notes: Note: SIRT6 activates PARP1 for DNA repair, distinct from PARP1's NAD+-draining role.

reactions.mechanism: SIRT6 binds RELA and deacetylates H3K9 at NF-kB target-gene promoters, attenuating NF-kB-dependent transcription; RelA haploinsufficiency rescues Sirt6-/- degeneration.
reactions.notes: Hyperactive NF-kB links SIRT6 loss to premature ageing.

reactions.mechanism: Transgenic SIRT6 overexpression extends lifespan (initially male mice, later both sexes) and reduces frailty, with lower IGF1 signalling and preserved energy homeostasis.
reactions.notes: Kanfi 2012 (males) + Roichman 2021 (both sexes, healthspan).

reactions.mechanism: The potent specific CD38 inhibitor 78c reverses age-related tissue NAD+ decline and improves glucose tolerance, muscle function, exercise capacity and cardiac function in aged mice; effects depend on NAD+ synthesis.
reactions.notes: Pharmacological validation of CD38 as an NAD+-boosting target.

reactions.mechanism: Resveratrol lowers the Km of SIRT1 for substrate and NAD+ and stimulates deacetylation of p53; activation is allosteric and depends on hydrophobic substrate motifs.
reactions.notes: CONFLICT: Pacholec (20061378) shows apparent activation is fluorophore/substrate-dependent, not with native substrates; Hubbard (23471411) reconciles via substrate hydrophobic motifs/E230. Kept as contested edge.

reactions.mechanism: Resveratrol competitively inhibits cAMP phosphodiesterases (PDE4), raising cAMP->Epac1->CamKKbeta, which activates AMPK and secondarily raises NAD+/SIRT1; PDE4 inhibition (rolipram) reproduces the metabolic benefits.
reactions.notes: Provides a SIRT1-independent route for resveratrol into the nutrient-sensing network.

reactions.mechanism: NMN supplementation restores NAD+ and improves insulin sensitivity: enhances muscle insulin signalling (AKT/mTOR) and glucose disposal in prediabetic women, and ameliorates glucose intolerance in diet-/age-induced diabetic mice.
reactions.notes: Yoshino 2021 is a randomized human trial (blood-readable outcome); Mills/Yoshino 2011 mouse support.

reactions.mechanism: Oral NR is uniquely bioavailable and produces dose-dependent increases in blood NAD+ metabolome in humans; chronic NR elevates NAD+ in middle-aged/older adults.
reactions.notes: Net NR->NAD+ (via NMRK1->NMN->NMNAT). CONFLICT: human physiological/clinical efficacy of raised NAD+ is limited (Vinten 2025, 41083806).

reactions.mechanism: Insulin binding stimulates dose-dependent phosphorylation of the 95 kDa beta-subunit of its own receptor, activating the receptor tyrosine kinase.
reactions.context: Human lymphocytes and rat hepatoma cells
reactions.notes: Classic demonstration of ligand-activated INSR autophosphorylation.

reactions.mechanism: Activated INSR tyrosine-kinase phosphorylates IRS1, which acts as a multisite docking protein binding SH2-domain signalling proteins including PI3K.
reactions.notes: Original IRS-1 cloning/characterisation.

reactions.mechanism: Tyrosine-phosphorylated IRS1 binds the SH2 domains of the p85 subunit of PI3K and activates PtdIns 3'-kinase; blocked by phosphotyrosine peptides.
reactions.notes: Connects to existing PI3K -> Akt edge in the map.

reactions.mechanism: IGF-1 binding stimulates a time- and dose-dependent tyrosine-specific kinase, the high-affinity IGF-1 receptor beta-subunit (distinct from insulin receptor).
reactions.notes: IGF1R structure defined by Ullrich 1986 (2877871).

reactions.mechanism: IGF-1/IGF1R stimulates tyrosine phosphorylation of IRS1, feeding the same PI3K-Akt cascade as insulin.
reactions.context: Hematopoietic and transfected cells; mouse lifespan genetics
reactions.notes: Aging relevance from Holzenberger 2003: Igf1r+/- mice live ~26% longer; establishes IGF1R axis as a mammalian lifespan regulator. | Merge review: PMID 7683417 only mentions IRS-1 as the IGF-I substrate in background and 12483226 supports IGF1R lifespan relevance, not the phosphorylation itself; needs a primary IGF1R->IRS1 citation.

reactions.mechanism: Akt phosphorylates FOXO3 (FKHRL1), promoting 14-3-3 binding and cytoplasmic retention, blocking its transcriptional activity.
reactions.notes: Aging context: FOXO3 variants strongly associated with human longevity (Willcox 2008; Flachsbart 2009).

reactions.mechanism: Nuclear FOXO3 transcribes autophagy genes (LC3, Bnip3, Gabarap, Atg12) to induce autophagy in skeletal muscle in vivo, independent of mTOR.
reactions.notes: Two independent labs (Sandri; Goldberg). Provides transcription-dependent route to the existing Autophagy node.

reactions.mechanism: Akt directly phosphorylates TSC2 (tuberin), destabilising it and disrupting the TSC1-TSC2 complex, relieving inhibition of mTORC1.
reactions.notes: Two independent groups (Guan; Cantley). Connects growth-factor signalling to existing TSC2 -| mTOR edge.

reactions.mechanism: TSC2 is a GTPase-activating protein toward RHEB, converting it to the inactive GDP-bound form and thereby suppressing mTORC1.
reactions.notes: Mechanistic basis for how TSC2 (existing node) controls mTOR.

reactions.mechanism: GTP-loaded RHEB binds the mTOR kinase domain and mLST8 and directly stimulates mTORC1 kinase activity toward S6K1 and 4E-BP1.
reactions.notes: Two groups (Avruch; Guan). RHEB is the obligatory mTORC1 activator.

reactions.mechanism: mTORC1 (RAFT1/FRAP/mTOR) directly phosphorylates p70 S6K1 on the rapamycin-sensitive T389 required for its kinase activity.
reactions.notes: Core mTORC1 output arm.

reactions.mechanism: mTORC1 phosphorylates 4E-BP1 on priming sites Thr37/Thr46 (two-step mechanism), enabling release of eIF4E and derepression of translation.
reactions.context: In vitro and in vivo, human cells
reactions.notes: Effect 'inhibition' = inhibition of 4E-BP1 repressor function. Two groups (Sonenberg; Sabatini).

reactions.mechanism: Hypophosphorylated 4E-BP1 binds eIF4E and blocks eIF4F assembly, inhibiting cap-dependent translation; mTORC1 phosphorylation relieves this.
reactions.notes: Translational-repressor output; sign is net inhibition of protein synthesis by 4E-BP1.

reactions.mechanism: Active S6K1 promotes translation of ribosomal/TOP mRNAs and translational efficiency, increasing protein synthesis downstream of mTORC1.
reactions.notes: Positive arm of mTORC1 translational output.

reactions.mechanism: S6K1 directly phosphorylates IRS1 on Ser1101, suppressing IRS1 tyrosine phosphorylation and downstream PI3K/Akt - a nutrient/insulin negative-feedback loop.
reactions.context: Mouse liver/muscle (db/db, high-fat diet) and human skeletal muscle amino-acid infusion
reactions.notes: Core mTOR-S6K1 feedback onto insulin signalling; Um 2004 ties it to age/diet-induced insulin resistance.

reactions.mechanism: S6K1 activity blunts insulin signalling via IRS1; S6K1-null mice are protected from age- and diet-induced insulin resistance and are long-lived.
reactions.notes: Selman 2009: S6K1 deletion extends lifespan and preserves insulin sensitivity; CR-mimetic transcriptome.

reactions.mechanism: mTORC1 on the lysosomal surface phosphorylates TFEB Ser211, promoting 14-3-3 binding and cytosolic retention; mTORC1 inhibition drives TFEB nuclear translocation.
reactions.notes: Two independent groups (Ballabio; Puertollano).

reactions.mechanism: Nuclear TFEB transcriptionally activates lysosomal and autophagy (CLEAR network) genes, increasing autophagic-lysosomal flux.
reactions.notes: Transcriptional route from mTORC1 inhibition to the existing Autophagy node.

reactions.mechanism: The rictor-mTOR complex (mTORC2) directly phosphorylates Akt on Ser473 in its hydrophobic motif and facilitates T308 phosphorylation, fully activating Akt.
reactions.notes: Second input to Akt besides PDK1/PI3K; relevant to rapamycin side-effects.

reactions.mechanism: Rapamycin, bound to FKBP12, binds mTOR (FRAP) and inhibits mTORC1 kinase activity toward S6K1/4E-BP1.
reactions.context: Mammalian cells; genetically heterogeneous mouse lifespan
reactions.notes: Harrison 2009: rapamycin extends lifespan even when started late in life - landmark pharmacological longevity result.

reactions.mechanism: Prolonged rapamycin treatment inhibits de novo mTORC2 assembly, reducing mTORC2 below the level needed to sustain Akt S473 phosphorylation in many cell types.
reactions.context: Multiple human cell lines, chronic treatment
reactions.notes: Explains off-target metabolic effects of chronic rapamycin.

reactions.mechanism: Chronic rapamycin disrupts mTORC2 in vivo, which is required for insulin-mediated suppression of hepatic gluconeogenesis; this causes glucose intolerance/insulin resistance, uncoupled from the longevity benefit.
reactions.notes: Conflict/nuance: decreased mTORC1 extends lifespan while mTORC2 loss impairs glucose homeostasis.

reactions.mechanism: AMPK directly phosphorylates PGC-1alpha at Thr177 and Ser538, required for PGC-1alpha-dependent induction of its own promoter and mitochondrial genes.
reactions.context: Primary mouse muscle cells and PGC-1alpha-null mice
reactions.notes: Links existing AMPK node to mitochondrial biogenesis.

reactions.mechanism: PGC-1alpha coactivates nuclear respiratory factors to drive mitochondrial gene expression and biogenesis; AMPK effects on mitochondrial genes are PGC-1alpha-dependent.
reactions.notes: Phenotype output of the AMPK-PGC-1alpha arm.

reactions.mechanism: Metformin accumulates in the mitochondrial matrix and causes time-dependent, self-limiting inhibition of respiratory-chain complex I, lowering cellular energy charge.
reactions.context: Hepatoma cells, isolated mitochondria, rat liver
reactions.notes: Primary molecular target of metformin; raises AMP:ATP to activate AMPK.

reactions.mechanism: Metformin activates AMPK in hepatocytes (via complex I inhibition/energy stress), reducing ACC activity and gluconeogenesis; required for its effect on hepatic glucose production.
reactions.notes: CONFLICT: Foretz 2010 (20577053) shows metformin lowers hepatic glucose production even without LKB1/AMPK, via energy state - AMPK is not strictly required for the glucose-lowering effect.

reactions.mechanism: Metformin raises circulating GDF15 (expressed in distal intestine and kidney); GDF15 acts on brainstem GFRAL to reduce food intake and body weight.
reactions.context: Two human RCTs and wild-type/knockout mice
reactions.notes: Blood-readable; GDF15/GFRAL needed for metformin's weight/energy-balance effect but not its glucose-lowering.

reactions.mechanism: Long-term metformin increases insulin sensitivity and AMPK activity and reduces oxidative damage/inflammation, mimicking some CR benefits.
reactions.notes: CONFLICT on lifespan: metformin improved healthspan/lifespan in Martin-Montalvo 2013, but metformin alone did NOT extend lifespan in the NIA ITP (Strong 2016, 27312235); only metformin+rapamycin did.

reactions.mechanism: DR lowers energy charge and activates AMPK, which acts (partly via FOXO/DAF-16) to extend lifespan and stress resistance.
reactions.context: C. elegans DR; conserved energy sensing
reactions.notes: AMPK required for DR lifespan extension (Greer 2007); mammalian CR induces AMPK-like transcriptome (Selman 2009).

reactions.mechanism: Calorie restriction reduces mTORC1 signalling (e.g. in Paneth cells of the intestinal stem-cell niche); the ISC-enhancing effect of CR is mimicked by rapamycin and abolished by forced mTORC1 activation.
reactions.context: Mouse intestine in vivo; C. elegans
reactions.notes: Two systems (mouse Yilmaz 2012; worm Hansen 2008) link DR to reduced TOR.

reactions.mechanism: Long-term CR markedly lowers fasting plasma insulin (and glucose) in humans practising calorie restriction.
reactions.notes: Blood-readable; part of reduced insulin/IGF signalling under DR.

reactions.mechanism: DR lowers serum IGF-1 in rodents; in humans IGF-1 is lowered only when protein intake is also restricted, not by CR alone.
reactions.notes: CONFLICT (kept): Fontana 2008 shows severe CR without protein restriction did NOT reduce IGF-1 in humans; protein intake is the key determinant. Edge sign holds for protein-restricted DR.

reactions.mechanism: CR induces SIRT1 expression in rat tissues and in human cells treated with serum from CR animals; insulin/IGF-1 attenuate this induction.
reactions.notes: Connects DR to existing SIRT1 node and NAD+ axis (axis A).

reactions.mechanism: DR and TOR inhibition induce autophagy; autophagy genes are required for DR/TOR-mediated lifespan extension (via PHA-4/FOXA).
reactions.notes: Autophagy necessary but not sufficient for DR longevity.

reactions.mechanism: Two years of 25% CR in non-obese adults (CALERIE RCT) significantly improved insulin sensitivity index and multiple cardiometabolic risk factors; CR also slowed the DunedinPACE pace of aging.
reactions.notes: Strongest human-intervention evidence; blood-readable outcome. Waziry 2023 slowed DunedinPACE (effect size small).

reactions.mechanism: Dietary protein restriction (not energy restriction) induces hepatic FGF21 expression via GCN2/eIF2alpha; FGF21 is required for the behavioural and metabolic responses to low-protein diet. Circulating FGF21 rose ~10-fold in rodents and markedly in humans after a low-protein diet.
reactions.context: Mouse/rat low-protein diet; 28-day human low-protein diet
reactions.notes: FGF21 is an endocrine signal of protein (amino-acid) restriction; GCN2-KO and FGF21-KO blunt the response. Energy-only restriction did NOT induce FGF21 here (see conflicts).

reactions.mechanism: During fasting and ketogenic diet, PPARalpha directly induces hepatic FGF21 transcription (PPARalpha binding by ChIP; PPARalpha agonists induce, Ppara-KO blunts). FGF21 then drives lipolysis, ketogenesis and the adaptive starvation response; adenoviral FGF21 knockdown causes fatty liver and reduced ketones.
reactions.notes: Two independent groups (Inagaki/Kliewer; Badman/Maratos-Flier) establish the PPARalpha-FGF21 axis as the fasting/ketotic inducer of FGF21.

reactions.mechanism: FGF21 requires the co-receptor betaKlotho (KLB), which physically binds FGFR1c (and FGFR2/3) to form the signalling complex that FGF21 activates (MAPK cascade, adipocyte glucose uptake). KLB knockdown abolishes FGF21 activity; tissue KLB+FGFR isoform expression dictates FGF21 target-tissue specificity.
reactions.context: Adipocytes (3T3-L1), heterologous receptor assays, mouse tissues
reactions.notes: Ogawa (PNAS) and Kurosu (JBC) independently define betaKlotho as the obligate FGF21 co-receptor with FGFR1c.

reactions.mechanism: Recombinant FGF21 increases AMPK phosphorylation in adipocytes and in white adipose tissue of ob/ob mice; the effect on mitochondrial function requires LKB1 (STK11), the upstream AMPK kinase.
reactions.notes: Connects FGF21 to the existing AMPK hub.

reactions.mechanism: FGF21 raises cellular NAD+ levels, thereby activating SIRT1 and deacetylation of its downstream targets (PGC-1alpha, histone 3) in adipocytes.
reactions.notes: FGF21 -> NAD+ -> SIRT1; ties the endocrine FGF21 arm into the NAD+/sirtuin module.

reactions.mechanism: Via the AMPK-SIRT1 axis FGF21 induces SIRT1-dependent deacetylation/activation of PGC-1alpha, enhancing mitochondrial oxygen consumption, citrate synthase activity and oxidative gene expression; inhibition of AMPK, SIRT1 or PGC-1alpha attenuates these effects.
reactions.notes: Downstream of AMPK/SIRT1; drives mitochondrial oxidative capacity (mitochondrial biogenesis arm).

reactions.mechanism: FGF21 causes hepatic GH resistance: it reduces active STAT5 and the expression of its target genes including IGF-1, and induces IGFBP1 and SOCS2 that blunt GH signalling; transcriptomics in FGF21-transgenic mice show blunted GH/IGF-1 signalling in liver.
reactions.notes: Links the FGF21 arm to the pro-longevity reduction of GH/IGF-1 signalling; supported by a mechanistic study and a lifespan study.

reactions.mechanism: Transgenic overexpression of FGF21 markedly extends median and maximal lifespan in mice without reducing food intake, acting primarily by blunting hepatic GH/IGF-1 signalling (independent of AMPK/mTOR/NAD+ markers).
reactions.notes: Genetic gain-of-function lifespan evidence.

reactions.mechanism: FGF21 reduces physical activity and promotes torpor, a regulated hypothermia/short-term hibernation-like state that conserves energy; FGF21-transgenic mice likewise show torpor.
reactions.notes: Mechanistic link from the FGF21 endocrine arm to the cold/low-body-temperature phenotype that DR also produces.

reactions.mechanism: FGF21 increases insulin sensitivity (FGF21-transgenic mice show insulin resistance improvement; recombinant FGF21 exerts antihyperglycaemic effects) through enhanced adipocyte glucose uptake and oxidative metabolism.
reactions.notes: Connects FGF21 to the existing Insulin_sensitivity phenotype.

reactions.mechanism: Semaglutide is a potent long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist; receptor agonism underlies its glucose-dependent insulinotropic, appetite-suppressing and cardiovascular actions demonstrated in large human RCTs.
reactions.notes: Pharmacological agonism; downstream effects captured in P1C-012/013.

reactions.mechanism: GLP-1R agonism suppresses appetite/food intake, producing sustained weight loss: 2.4 mg weekly semaglutide gave -14.9% body weight vs -2.4% placebo at 68 weeks with improved cardiometabolic risk factors (STEP 1).
reactions.context: Human RCT, adults with overweight/obesity without diabetes
reactions.notes: Food-intake reduction is the proximal mechanism; body weight used as the phenotype node.

reactions.mechanism: In 17,604 patients with pre-existing CVD and overweight/obesity but no diabetes, weekly semaglutide reduced the composite of CV death, nonfatal MI or nonfatal stroke (6.5% vs 8.0%; HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.72-0.90) over ~40 months (SELECT).
reactions.notes: Blood-prevention-relevant age-associated clinical outcome of GLP-1R agonism.

reactions.mechanism: Canagliflozin inhibits the renal sodium/glucose cotransporter SGLT2 (SLC5A2), blocking proximal-tubule glucose reabsorption and producing glucosuria and lower blood glucose.
reactions.notes: Primary on-target action of canagliflozin.

reactions.mechanism: Independently of SGLT2, canagliflozin inhibits mitochondrial respiratory complex I, raising cellular AMP/ADP and activating AMPK (at plasma concentrations seen clinically); downstream ACC1/2 phosphorylation lowers lipid synthesis. Effect is AMPK-dependent (absent in AMPK-KO cells) and occurs in mouse liver in vivo.
reactions.context: HEK293/cell lines; mouse liver in vivo
reactions.notes: Off-target AMPK activation distinguishes canagliflozin from dapagliflozin/empagliflozin; connects SGLT2i to the AMPK hub (shared with metformin-like action).

reactions.mechanism: By blocking renal glucose reuptake (and reducing hyperglycaemia generally), canagliflozin lowers fasting glucose and improves glucose tolerance in both sexes of mice; blunting of daily peak glucose is proposed to mediate its lifespan benefit (parallel to acarbose).
reactions.notes: Glucose-lowering is the proposed longevity mechanism and connects to the Glucose nutrient node.

reactions.mechanism: In the NIA Interventions Testing Program, chow canagliflozin (180 ppm from 7 months) extended median survival of male genetically heterogeneous mice by 14% and raised 90th-percentile age by 9%, consistently across 3 sites; no lifespan benefit in females despite improved glucose handling in both sexes.
reactions.notes: Male-specific lifespan extension; strong sex conflict (see conflicts). Single PMID but multi-site ITP.

reactions.mechanism: Caloric restriction decreased survival of aged mice after primary influenza infection, with increased lung virus titers and reduced NK-cell activity, despite preserved mitogen-induced lymphoproliferation; i.e. CR impairs the primary antiviral response in aged hosts.
reactions.context: Aged CR mice, primary influenza challenge (review corroboration)
reactions.notes: Adverse effect of DR; Wang 2025 review corroborates increased infection vulnerability under CR.

reactions.mechanism: Long-term CR lowers core body temperature in humans: 24-h telemetric core temperature was significantly lower in people practising ~6 years of CR than in Western-diet or exercise-matched controls, independent of leanness. Sustained CALERIE CR produced metabolic adaptation with reduced thyroid-axis (T3) activity, the endocrine basis of lower heat production.
reactions.notes: Lower body temperature is both a proposed longevity mediator and an adverse comfort/cold-tolerance cost; Conti & de Cabo 2025 (PMID 40205073, review) further argues lowered T contributes to CR anti-aging.

reactions.mechanism: Review synthesis (primarily rodent, some human data): calorie restriction downregulates energy-demanding processes including tissue repair, slowing/impairing wound healing as part of a trade-off prioritising survival functions.
reactions.context: Rodent studies summarised in review; some human data
reactions.notes: Review-only support (no primary rodent PMID located during curation that cleanly isolates a longevity-type DR regimen; protein-energy malnutrition literature is adjacent). Kept at low confidence per brief's request to include DR adverse effects.

reactions.mechanism: mTOR inhibition by sirolimus/rapalogs impairs wound healing in transplant recipients: a prospective RCT found sirolimus-based regimens caused high rates of wound complications (lymphocele 32%, dehiscence 10% when steroids co-administered), and benefit-risk reviews list impaired wound healing and lymphocele formation among sirolimus adverse effects (antiproliferative action on repairing tissue).
reactions.notes: Conflict: Dutt 2017 (PMID 28405603) found everolimus did NOT delay closure of small 3-mm punch-biopsy wounds in non-diabetic transplant patients; severity appears wound-size/dose/comorbidity dependent.

reactions.mechanism: mTOR inhibition ameliorates immunosenescence: the rapalog RAD001 (everolimus) enhanced the elderly influenza-vaccine antibody response by ~20% and reduced the fraction of PD-1+ CD4/CD8 T cells in a placebo-controlled RCT, a beneficial immune effect of mTOR inhibition.
reactions.notes: Beneficial (not adverse) effect of mTOR inhibition; included as Rapamycin/mTOR -> immune-function phenotype as the brief allowed when supported. Opposes the wound-healing harm (same drug, opposite sign).

conflicts: Resveratrol as a direct SIRT1 activator is contested: Howitz 2003 (12939617) reported direct activation, but Pacholec 2010 (20061378) showed activation is an artifact of fluorophore-tagged substrates and absent with native substrates; Hubbard 2013 (23471411) reconciles by showing activation requires hydrophobic substrate motifs and SIRT1-E230, i.e. substrate-assisted allosteric activation. Resveratrol also acts SIRT1-independently via PDE4/AMPK (Park 2012, 22304913).

Human efficacy of NAD+ precursors is limited and the human age-related NAD+ decline itself is inconsistently observed: NR reliably raises blood NAD+ (Trammell 2016, Martens 2018) and NMN improves muscle insulin sensitivity in one RCT (Yoshino 2021), but Vinten 2025 (41083806, review) concludes clinical/physiological benefits and the evidence for a systemic human NAD+ decline remain weak and tissue-specific. Edges P1A-032/P1A-033 are scored with this caveat.

NAD+ is double-edged for cancer prevention: NAMPT-driven NAD+ biosynthesis supports tumour-cell proliferation, stress tolerance and immune evasion, making NAMPT/PARP inhibition anticancer strategies (Arrizabalaga 2026, 42880252, review; also flagged in Rajman 2018). Thus boosting NAD+ for ageing may conflict with cancer-prevention goals; captured here as a conflict pending a primary paper tied to a specific map node.

PARP1 appears with opposite signs: as a bulk NAD+ consumer it lowers NAD+/SIRT1 (P1A-007/P1A-008, Bai 2011), yet SIRT6 activates PARP1 to promote DNA-repair under stress (P1A-026, Mao 2011). Both are retained because they operate in different contexts (chronic NAD+ drain vs. acute genotoxic repair).

Metformin -> AMPK (P1B-026): Zhou 2001 establishes AMPK activation as the mechanism, but Foretz 2010 shows metformin still lowers hepatic glucose production in LKB1/AMPK-null hepatocytes via a fall in energy charge - AMPK is not strictly required for the glucose-lowering effect.

Metformin healthspan/lifespan (P1B-028): Martin-Montalvo 2013 reports improved healthspan/lifespan and insulin sensitivity in mice at 0.1% diet (1% was toxic), whereas the NIA Interventions Testing Program (Strong 2016) found metformin alone did not significantly extend lifespan; only metformin+rapamycin did.

Dietary_restriction -| IGF1 (P1B-032): robust in rodents, but Fontana 2008 shows severe CR without protein restriction did NOT lower serum IGF-1 in humans - protein intake, not calories, is the key determinant. Edge sign holds only for protein-restricted DR.

Rapamycin: beneficial mTORC1 inhibition (lifespan, Harrison 2009) is partly uncoupled from detrimental mTORC2 disruption (insulin resistance, Lamming 2012 / Sarbassov 2006) - same drug, opposite-sign metabolic vs longevity outcomes (P1B-020/021/022).

CALERIE human CR (Waziry 2023): slowed DunedinPACE pace-of-aging but did NOT significantly change PhenoAge/GrimAge clocks; treatment effect sizes small - human CR benefit on biological age is real but modest (P1B-035).

FGF21 induction is nutrient-specific: Laeger 2014 shows hepatic FGF21 is induced by PROTEIN (amino-acid) restriction and NOT by energy-only restriction, whereas Inagaki 2007 and Badman 2007 show acute fasting/ketogenic diet induce FGF21 via PPARalpha. Thus FGF21 marks protein restriction and acute starvation but may not rise under chronic energy restriction with adequate protein — both edges (P1C-001, P1C-002) kept.

Canagliflozin extends median lifespan in MALE but not FEMALE genetically heterogeneous mice (Miller 2020), despite improving glucose handling in both sexes — a strong sex-by-treatment interaction (P1C-017).

mTOR inhibition shows opposite-sign effects: it impairs wound healing in some clinical settings (Sandrini 2008 RCT: elevated lymphocele/dehiscence; Kuypers 2005 review) yet improves elderly immune/vaccine response (Mannick 2014). Edges P1C-021 and P1C-022 therefore carry opposite effects for the same intervention.

Rapamycin/everolimus wound-healing harm is context-dependent: Dutt 2017 found everolimus did NOT delay closure of small 3-mm punch-biopsy wounds in non-diabetic transplant patients, conflicting with the larger-wound/lymphocele complication data — severity depends on wound size, dose and comorbidity (e.g. diabetes).

Dietary restriction is simultaneously pro-longevity and carries adverse costs within this axis: increased primary-infection mortality in aged mice (Gardner 2005), lowered core body temperature/cold sensitivity (Soare 2011; Redman 2018), and review-level impaired wound healing (Wang 2025) — the latter also being a proposed longevity mediator (lower body temperature; Conti 2025).

dropped.edge: NAMPT/NAD+ -> tumour cell survival (pro-cancer double edge)
dropped.reason: Only review-level sources found within scope (Arrizabalaga 2026 42880252; Rajman 2018 review). Per rule 3 no primary perturbation paper located for a specific node, so recorded as a conflict rather than a curated edge.
Optional edge; could not verify a correct primary PMID within the search budget (a candidate PMID returned an unrelated article), so dropped rather than cite an unchecked PMID.
Verified and real, but outside the NAD+/sirtuin salvage sub-axis scope (kinase regulation of SIRT1); omitted to stay within ~30 core edges.

Conflicting mammalian data: Martin-Montalvo 2013 shows lifespan extension in male mice, but NIA ITP (Strong 2016) found metformin alone did not extend lifespan. Encoded instead at the metformin species level and as healthspan/insulin-sensitivity edge P1B-028 with the conflict noted; Lifespan_extension reserved for unambiguous genetic/mouse data per brief.
Captured via RPS6KB1 species aging_relevance and the RPS6KB1 -| Insulin_sensitivity edge (P1B-016, Selman 2009); avoided a redundant phenotype edge.

Textbook incretin action but no primary mechanistic PMID verified within this axis, and it is peripheral to the aging/blood-prevention focus; omitted to avoid an under-supported edge. GLP-1R agonism is instead captured via weight (P1C-012) and cardiovascular (P1C-013) outcomes.

Foundational and true, but no specific primary PMID could be verified during curation (candidate PMID was incorrect on lookup) and the existing NSCLC map already represents mTOR regulation; rapamycin is connected via its phenotype edges (P1C-021 wound healing, P1C-022 vaccine response) instead. Mechanism text notes mTORC1 inhibition.

No clean primary rodent study isolating a longevity-type DR regimen (vs protein-energy malnutrition) was located; retained at low confidence as a review-only edge (P1C-020) rather than dropped, per the brief's request to represent DR adverse effects.
